new_words.english_meaning: A pre-arranged meeting point or time agreed upon by a group before an outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: પહેલેથી નક્કી કરેલ મળવાની જગ્યા અથવા સમય — જ્યાં બધા ભેગા થવાના હોય.
new_words.usage_note: Borrowed from French; used in both military and casual social contexts for a planned meeting spot.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Rendezvous' = ભેગા થવાની જગ્યા → picnic પહેલાં ક્યાં મળવું તે નક્કી કરવું.
examples: Our rendezvous before the picnic is the park's main entrance at ten.
They chose the old oak tree as their rendezvous point.
Make sure everyone knows the rendezvous time so nobody gets left behind.
The group missed their rendezvous because of heavy traffic.

new_words.english_meaning: An arrangement where several people share one vehicle for a trip, splitting travel costs and effort.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: એક ગોઠવણ જેમાં ઘણા લોકો એક જ ગાડીમાં સાથે મુસાફરી કરે છે અને ખર્ચ વહેંચે છે.
new_words.usage_note: Very common in American English; also used as a verb — 'We carpooled to the event.'
new_words.memory_tip: 'Car' + 'pool' = ગાડીઓ ભેગી કરવી → carpool = ઘણા જણ એક ગાડીમાં.
examples: We decided to carpool to the picnic to save on parking fees.
Arranging a carpool made the outing much more affordable for everyone.
She volunteered to drive the carpool since her SUV had the most space.
The carpool left at eight sharp, so don't be late!

new_words.english_meaning: A count of the total number of people attending or present at an event.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઇવેન્ટ કે ભ્રમણમાં આવનારા અથવા હાજર વ્યક્તિઓની કુલ સંખ્યાની ગણતરી.
new_words.usage_note: Typically used before an event to plan food and logistics, or after to confirm all members are present.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Head' = માથું → headcount = માથા ગણવા → કેટલા લોકો આવ્યા?
examples: Can you do a headcount before we order the food?
The final headcount was thirty-two, more than we expected.
Always take a headcount before leaving the picnic site.
She sent a message asking for a headcount so she could book the right number of seats.

new_words.english_meaning: To reply to an invitation confirming whether you will or will not attend an event.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: આમંત્રણનો જવાબ આપવો — જણાવવું કે તમે આવશો કે નહીં.
new_words.usage_note: From French 'répondez s'il vous plaît'; now used as a verb in everyday English.
new_words.memory_tip: 'RSVP' = જવાબ આપો → picnic invite આવ્યું? RSVP કરો — 'હા' અથવા 'ના' કહો.
examples: Please RSVP by Thursday so we know how much food to bring.
Only half the group RSVP'd, which made planning difficult.
She forgot to RSVP and almost missed the outing.
We need everyone to RSVP before we can confirm the venue booking.

new_words.english_meaning: A meal or gathering where each guest contributes a dish of food to share with everyone.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: એક ભોજન-સભા જ્યાં દરેક ભાગ લેનાર પોતાની ડિશ લઈ આવે અને બધા મળી ખાય.
collocations: bring a dish for the potluck
new_words.usage_note: A potluck picnic is a popular, budget-friendly way to share a variety of foods without one person bearing all the cost.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Pot' = વાસણ + 'luck' = નસીબ → potluck = દરેક ઘરમાંથી ડિશ લઈ આવે → ભાતભાતની વાનગી.
examples: We decided to have a potluck picnic so everyone could bring their favourite dish.
She brought a big bowl of pasta salad to the potluck.
Potluck gatherings are a great way to try different home-cooked foods.
The potluck was a hit — there was something for everyone.

new_words.english_meaning: The act of visiting potential locations in advance to decide if they are suitable for an outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઓટ્ટિંગ માટે અગાઉ સ્થળ જોઈ આવવું — યોગ્ય છે કે નહીં તે ચકાસવા.
new_words.usage_note: Often used as 'scout out a location' — checking a place before committing to it for the group.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Scout' = ખોળવા નીકળવું → scouting = picnic ની જગ્યા અગાઉ જોઈ આવવી.
examples: We went scouting for the perfect spot near the lake last weekend.
A bit of location scouting saved us from choosing a crowded site.
He scouted out three different parks before settling on one.
Scouting the area ahead of time means no surprises on the day.

new_words.english_meaning: A backup plan made in case something goes wrong, such as bad weather cancelling an outdoor event.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: અણધારી ઘટના — જેમ કે ખરાબ હવામાન — ના સ્થિતિ માટે પહેલેથી તૈયાર કરેલ વૈકલ્પિક યોજના.
new_words.usage_note: Essential for outdoor events; commonly paired with 'in case of rain' or 'if the weather turns'.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Contingency' = અણધારી ઘટના → contingency plan = 'Plan B' — વરસાદ આવે તો ઘરે.
examples: Always have a contingency plan in case the weather ruins your picnic.
Our contingency plan was to move the gathering to the community hall.
She appreciated that the organiser had thought of a contingency plan for rain.
A good contingency plan keeps everyone relaxed even if things go wrong.

new_words.english_meaning: To organise and manage different people or activities so they work together smoothly for an event.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઇવેન્ટ સારી રીતે ચાલે તે માટે જુદા-જુદા લોકો અને કામોને ગોઠવવા અને સંચાલિત કરવા.
new_words.usage_note: Used when one person takes the lead in managing schedules, transport, and food for a group outing.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Co' = સાથે + 'ordinate' = ક્રમ → coordinate = બધું ક્રમમાં ગોઠવવું.
examples: She offered to coordinate the whole picnic so nobody else had to worry.
It takes real skill to coordinate a large group outing smoothly.
He coordinated the transport, food, and activities for the day.
Good coordination means the event runs without a hitch.

new_words.english_meaning: An estimate or plan of how much money will be spent on an outing and how it will be allocated.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઓટ્ટિંગ પર કેટલો ખર્ચ થશે અને ક્યાં-ક્યાં ખર્ચ વહેંચવો — એ અંગેનો અંદાજ અને આયોજન.
new_words.usage_note: Setting a budget per person prevents disagreements about spending after the outing.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Budget' = ખર્ચ-આયોજન → picnic budget = ખોરાક, ગાડી, ટિકિટ — બધા માટે ગણવું.
examples: We set a strict budget of five hundred rupees per person for the outing.
Keeping within budget meant we had to skip the boat ride.
She created a shared spreadsheet to track the picnic budget.
A clear budget stops arguments about who owes what after the trip.

new_words.english_meaning: A list of planned activities or events in order for the day of the outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઓટ્ટિંગ ના દિવસ માટે ક્રમ અનુસાર ગોઠવેલ પ્રવૃત્તિઓ અથવા ઘટનાઓની યાદી.
new_words.usage_note: While 'agenda' is often used in business meetings, it is equally useful for planning a structured day out.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Agenda' = શું-શું કરવું — ક્રમ અનુસાર → picnic agenda = સવારે નીકળો, બપોરે ખાઓ, સાંજે રમો.
examples: The agenda for the day included a nature walk, lunch, and games.
She shared the agenda on the group chat so everyone was prepared.
Having a clear agenda kept the outing on track.
The agenda was flexible — they could change activities if people wanted.

new_words.english_meaning: An insulated box used to keep food and drinks cold during an outdoor outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઠંડા ખોરાક અને પીણાં જાળવી રાખવા માટેનો ઇન્સ્યૂલેટેડ બૉક્સ — picnic વખતે ઉપયોગ.
new_words.usage_note: Called a 'cool box' in British English; usually packed with ice or reusable ice packs.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Cool' = ઠંડું → cooler = ઠંડું રાખવાવાળું બૉક્સ → picnic ની ઠંડી cold drink.
examples: We packed the cooler with sandwiches, fruit, and cold juice.
Don't forget to put ice in the cooler before you leave home.
The cooler kept the watermelon perfectly chilled all afternoon.
He lugged the heavy cooler all the way to the picnic spot.

new_words.english_meaning: A large, heavy-duty waterproof sheet used as ground cover or shelter during outdoor activities.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: મોટું, ટકાઉ, વૉટરપ્રૂફ કપડું — જમીન ઉપર પાથરવા અથવા વરસાદ સામે રક્ષણ માટે.
new_words.usage_note: Often shortened to 'tarp' in everyday speech; essential for sitting on damp grass or making a rain cover.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Tarpaulin' → tarp = ભેજ અને ગંદકીથી બચાવ → picnic માં ઘાસ પર બેસો, ભીં ન થાઓ.
examples: They spread a large tarpaulin under the trees before sitting down.
The tarpaulin doubled as a rain shelter when the clouds rolled in.
Always carry a tarp — the ground can be damp even on sunny days.
She weighted the corners of the tarpaulin with stones so it wouldn't blow away.

new_words.english_meaning: A lotion or cream applied to the skin to protect it from the sun's ultraviolet rays.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ત્વચા પર લગાડવાની ક્રીમ — જે સૂર્યના નુકસાનકારક અલ્ટ્રાવાયોલેટ કિરણોથી રક્ષણ આપે.
new_words.usage_note: Dermatologists recommend SPF 30 or higher; must be reapplied every two hours when outdoors.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Sun' = સૂર્ય + 'screen' = ઢાંકવું → sunscreen = સૂર્યથી ત્વચા ઢાંકો.
examples: She reminded everyone to apply sunscreen before heading out to the meadow.
Always pack sunscreen, especially for summer picnics.
He forgot his sunscreen and ended up with a painful sunburn.
Reapply sunscreen every two hours for the best protection.

new_words.english_meaning: A spray or lotion that keeps insects such as mosquitoes away from the skin during outdoor activities.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: એક સ્પ્રે અથવા ક્રીમ — જે બહારે ફરતી વખતે મચ્છર વગેરે જીવડાઓને દૂર રાખે.
new_words.usage_note: Essential for picnics near water or in wooded areas; DEET-based sprays are the most effective.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Repellent' = ભગાડવું → insect repellent = જીવડાઓ ભગાડો → picnic ખૂબ આરામ.
examples: Don't go near the pond without insect repellent — the mosquitoes are terrible.
She packed two bottles of insect repellent for the forest picnic.
Apply insect repellent on exposed skin before sitting in the grass.
A good insect repellent can save your picnic from being ruined by bugs.

new_words.english_meaning: A vacuum-insulated container that keeps liquids hot or cold for several hours.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ઇન્સ્યૂલેટેડ ડબ્બો — જે ઘણા કલાકો સુધી પ્રવાહી ગરમ અથવા ઠંડું રાખે.
new_words.usage_note: 'Thermos' is a brand name that has become a generic term; 'vacuum flask' is the technical alternative.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Thermos' = ગરમ-ઠંડું બચાવ → picnic ઉપર ગરમ ચા ઠંડી ન થાય — thermos ભરી લો.
examples: She brought a thermos of masala chai to enjoy in the cool morning air.
Pack a thermos of hot soup if the weather turns chilly.
The thermos kept the coffee piping hot for six hours.
He unscrewed the thermos lid and poured a steaming cup for everyone.

new_words.english_meaning: A lightweight portable table that folds flat for easy carrying and storage during outings.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: હળવો, વહન-સૂક્ષ્મ ટેબલ — જે ફ્લૅટ ફોલ્ડ થઈ જાય, picnic માટે સરળ.
new_words.usage_note: Often paired with folding chairs; makes outdoor dining much more comfortable for groups.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Folding' = ફોલ્ડ થવું → folding table = ફોલ્ડ થઈ ગાડીમાં આવી જાય — picnic ready!
examples: We set up a folding table so the kids had somewhere to eat comfortably.
The folding table made serving food so much easier than balancing plates on our laps.
He unfolded the table in seconds and placed it under the shade tree.
A folding table is worth its weight in gold at a large family picnic.

new_words.english_meaning: Pre-moistened disposable cloths used for cleaning hands or surfaces when water is not available outdoors.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ભીના, ek-use, disposable કપડા — બહારે પાણી ન હોય ત્યારે હાથ અથવા સપાટી સાફ કરવા.
new_words.usage_note: An absolute picnic essential — useful for sticky fingers, spills, and when hand sanitiser is not enough.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Wet' = ભીનું + 'wipes' = લૂ → wet wipes = picnic ઉppar hath saf karo, pani vaghar.
examples: She handed out wet wipes after the kids finished their sticky mango slices.
Always pack a large pack of wet wipes for outdoor meals.
He used a wet wipe to clean the folding table before setting out the food.
Wet wipes saved the day when someone spilled juice on their shirt.

new_words.english_meaning: A durable bag made to be used many times, replacing single-use plastic bags when carrying picnic items.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ટકાઉ બૅગ — જે વારંવાર વાપરી શકાય, plastic bag ના બદલે picnic નો સામાન લઈ જવા.
new_words.usage_note: Encouraged for environmental reasons; large canvas tote bags are popular for carrying picnic supplies.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Reusable' = ફ-repeatedly-use → reusable bag = ek-bar-not, vari-vari vaapar — eco-friendly.
examples: She carried all the food in a large reusable bag to avoid plastic waste.
Pack everything into reusable bags — it's better for the environment.
They used colourful reusable bags to sort food, games, and first-aid supplies.
A sturdy reusable bag can carry far more than a flimsy plastic one.

new_words.english_meaning: A small bag or box containing basic medical supplies for treating minor injuries during outings.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: નાની kit — picnic ઉppar minor injuries — cuts, burns, blisters — ની first treatment મા.
new_words.usage_note: Should include bandages, antiseptic wipes, pain relief tablets, and tweezers at minimum for outdoor trips.
new_words.memory_tip: 'First-aid' = first-help → picnic ness chhoti-injuries → first-aid kit = instant relief.
examples: Always pack a first-aid kit when heading outdoors, especially with children.
She used the first-aid kit to treat a small cut he got climbing a fence.
The first-aid kit had everything they needed for his bee sting.
A basic first-aid kit is non-negotiable on any outdoor outing.

new_words.english_meaning: A battery-powered device that can recharge mobile phones and other electronics while away from a power outlet.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: battery-powered gadget — picnic ness power-socket vaghar phone charge kari shake.
new_words.usage_note: Also known as a 'power bank'; essential for all-day outings when phones are used for navigation and photos.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Portable' = carry-able → portable charger = kahie-pana phone charge karo — power bank.
examples: His portable charger saved them when Google Maps drained the phone battery.
Pack a fully charged portable charger for long outdoor trips.
She shared her portable charger so everyone could take photos all day.
Without a portable charger, they would have had no way to call for a taxi.

new_words.english_meaning: A covering of branches and leaves formed by tree tops, or an overhead portable shelter at an outdoor spot.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: વૃક્ષોની ટોચ ઉppar-thi banel branch-leaf-ni natural chhatri — picnic ness shade aape.
new_words.usage_note: In a picnic context refers both to the natural tree canopy above and to portable pop-up shelters.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Canopy' = upper cover → tree canopy = trees-ni natural chhatri → picnic ness dhoop na laage.
examples: They spread their blanket beneath the cool green canopy of the mango trees.
The forest canopy filtered the sunlight into beautiful dappled patterns on the ground.
A pop-up canopy is useful when there are no trees for shade.
Sitting under the canopy, they barely noticed how hot the afternoon had become.

new_words.english_meaning: The summit or highest point of a hill, often offering wide open views of the surrounding landscape.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ટેકરીનો સૌથી ઊppar-no bhag — aw-vast views mile — picnic mast spot.
new_words.usage_note: A popular picnic setting for the scenic views; the climb up is considered part of the experience.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Hill' = ટેકરી + 'top' = ઉppar → hilltop = tekri-no upar-bhag → view dhamo!
examples: They hiked up to the hilltop and spread their blanket to enjoy the sweeping views.
A hilltop picnic at sunset is one of the most romantic experiences.
The hilltop was breezy and cool, a perfect escape from the city heat.
You can see three villages from the hilltop on a clear day.

new_words.english_meaning: An area of land planted with fruit trees, often a scenic and shaded spot for a relaxed outdoor meal.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: ફળ-વૃક્ષોથી ભરેલ જમીન-no bhag — picnic mast shady spot — fruits-ni sugandhhi vaatavaran.
new_words.usage_note: A picnic in an orchard during blossom or harvest season is a particularly memorable experience.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Orchard' = aw-fruit garden → orchard-maa picnic = aw-shade + aw-fresh fruits.
examples: They laid their blanket in the cool shade of the old mango orchard.
The orchard was in full bloom, making it the perfect backdrop for the picnic.
Children love running between the trees in an orchard.
She picked a few fallen apples from the orchard to add to the picnic spread.

new_words.english_meaning: An area of land or a promenade situated directly beside a body of water such as a lake, river, or sea.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: તળાવ, નદી, અથવા સમુદ્ર-ની સીધ-ni-sathe-ni jameen — scenic picnic spot.
new_words.usage_note: Often a public park or promenade area; ideal for picnics as the breeze from the water keeps things cool.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Water' = પાણી + 'front' = સામ-ni-side → waterfront = paani-ni saame ni jameen.
examples: The city's waterfront park was the perfect place for their Sunday picnic.
They sat on the waterfront, watching the boats drift by as they ate.
A waterfront picnic spot always has a refreshing breeze.
The waterfront was busy with families enjoying the sunny afternoon.

new_words.english_meaning: Rural land outside towns and cities, typically featuring open fields, farmland, and natural scenery.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: શહેર-ner-thi-door-na gramin vistar — khuli khet, kheti, ane prakruti-ni sundarata.
new_words.usage_note: Used as an uncountable noun in most contexts — 'the countryside' rather than 'a countryside'.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Country' = gramin + 'side' = baar-no vistar → countryside = sheher-thi door prakruti.
examples: Nothing beats a picnic in the open countryside on a warm spring day.
They drove an hour out of the city to reach the rolling countryside.
The children loved exploring the countryside, spotting birds and wildflowers.
The countryside air felt so fresh after weeks spent in the city.

new_words.english_meaning: A small, still body of fresh water, smaller than a lake, often found in parks or countryside settings.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: નાનો, સ્ÿ-still, swacchhh-paani-no jhil — park ke graamin vistar-maa mole.
new_words.usage_note: A pond is smaller than a lake and usually shallower; park ponds often have ducks and are popular picnic spots.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Pond' = aw-small lake → duck pond-na-kinare picnic = shaant vataavaran.
examples: The children fed the ducks at the pond while the adults set out the picnic.
They found a shady spot right beside the duck pond.
The reflection of the trees on the still pond was breathtaking.
A picnic by the pond is the most peaceful way to spend a Sunday afternoon.

new_words.english_meaning: An open field covered with naturally growing wild flowers, creating a colourful and scenic picnic backdrop.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: khulaa maidan-maa kude-kude aw-naturally ugeli jangli phulvadi — rang-birangi ane sundar.
new_words.usage_note: Seasonal — most spectacular in spring and early summer; common in hill stations and national parks across India.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Wild' = jangli + 'flower' = phul + 'field' = maidan → wildflower field = jangli phulwadi.
examples: They spread their blanket in the middle of a stunning wildflower field.
The wildflower field smelled incredible on the warm spring afternoon.
She took dozens of photos of the children playing in the wildflower field.
A wildflower field in full bloom is one of nature's greatest spectacles.

new_words.english_meaning: The very top edge of a steep rock face, offering dramatic views but requiring caution.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-steep paharadi-no sadam kinaro — dramatic views — paran dhyan-thi.
collocations: picnic with a cliff edge view
new_words.usage_note: Picnics near cliff edges should be approached with caution; keep children and pets safely back from the edge.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Cliff' = aw-pahari-kinaro + 'edge' = kinaaro → cliff edge = aw-upar-no pahari-kinaro.
examples: They set up their picnic just back from the cliff edge to admire the coastal views safely.
The cliff edge offered an uninterrupted view of the ocean for miles.
Children were kept well away from the cliff edge during the outing.
A light breeze blew in from the sea as they sat near the cliff edge.

new_words.english_meaning: A path or road surfaced with small rounded stones, often found in old town gardens and historic outdoor spaces.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: gol-gol nana pathharaa-thi bnaeli vaat — purani garden ya historic jaga-maa mole.
new_words.usage_note: Often associated with heritage gardens and old European-style parks; adds a picturesque quality to an outing.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Cobblestone' = gol-gol pathhar + 'path' = vaat → cobblestone path = purani pathar-wali vaat.
examples: They strolled along the cobblestone path to find the perfect picnic spot.
The cobblestone path through the heritage garden was lined with rose bushes.
Watch your step on the cobblestone path — it can be slippery when wet.
The cobblestone path added a charming old-world feel to their afternoon outing.

new_words.english_meaning: An open space within a forest where trees are absent, often filled with grass and natural light.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: jungle-ni-vaache-no khulo maidan — jyaa vraksh nathi — ghass ane prakash bharyo.
new_words.usage_note: A poetic and literary word for a clearing in the woods; used in nature writing and travel descriptions.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Glade' = jungle-ni-vaache khulo bhag → glade-maa picnic = shade + light + prakriti.
examples: They discovered a beautiful sunlit glade at the heart of the forest.
The glade was carpeted with soft grass — the perfect picnic spot.
Birdsong filled the peaceful glade as they unpacked their lunch.
A glade feels magical — surrounded by trees yet open to the sky.

new_words.english_meaning: A lightweight plastic disc thrown and caught between players as an outdoor recreational game.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-halku plastic disc — players vaache pheki-pakdi — picnic outdoor game.
new_words.usage_note: 'Frisbee' is a brand name; 'flying disc' is the generic term. A classic picnic activity for all ages.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Frisbee' = aw-gol disc — pheko, pakdo → picnic-ni-mast outdoor game.
examples: The kids spent hours throwing the frisbee across the open lawn.
A frisbee is the easiest game to pack for a day out — it weighs almost nothing.
They organised a friendly frisbee tournament after lunch.
Even the dog joined in the frisbee game, leaping to catch it mid-air.

new_words.english_meaning: The recreational activity of flying a kite in the open air, typically done in breezy open spaces.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: khuli hava-maa patang-udaadavani kriya — breeze-no faydo uthaavine masti karo.
new_words.usage_note: Best done in open fields or hills where there are no trees or power lines to snag the kite string.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Kite' = patang → kite-flying = patang udaadvanu → Uttarayan jaisi masti picnic-maa.
examples: The wide-open field was perfect for kite-flying after their picnic lunch.
She taught her nephew how to launch a kite for the first time.
Kite-flying is one of those timeless activities the whole family enjoys.
The sky above the park was dotted with colourful kites all afternoon.

new_words.english_meaning: A game where participants search for a list of specific items or complete tasks in an outdoor setting.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-game — jyaa badhaa log yaadi-maa-apela items-ni khoj kare — outdoor setting-maa.
new_words.usage_note: A nature scavenger hunt — finding specific leaves, stones, or birds — is a great way to engage children outdoors.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Scavenger' = khaajvaalavaa + 'hunt' = khojavanu → scavenger hunt = items-ni masti khoj.
examples: She prepared a nature scavenger hunt list for the children to complete during the picnic.
The scavenger hunt kept the kids busy and excited for hours.
Teams competed to finish the scavenger hunt before the sun set.
Finding all the items on the scavenger hunt list felt like a real adventure.

new_words.english_meaning: Wading in shallow water, usually a stream or the sea, as a leisurely outdoor activity.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-uttla paani-maa-chalavanu — nadi ke dariya-na kinare — shaant ane anandmay kriya.
new_words.usage_note: A very British activity — rolling up trousers and wading into a shallow stream or the sea at the seaside.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Paddle' = uttlaa paani-maa chaalvu → paddling = picnic-na kinare paani-maa-ramvu.
examples: The children went paddling in the cool stream while the adults relaxed on the bank.
She rolled up her jeans and joined the kids for a spot of paddling.
Paddling in the shallow river was the highlight of their countryside outing.
On hot days, paddling in cool water is the perfect outdoor activity.

new_words.english_meaning: A leisurely walk taken in a natural outdoor setting to observe and appreciate wildlife and scenery.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: prakruti-maa-chalavanu — pakshio, phuldo, ane vaatavaran joi aanand levanu — shaant bhramriti.
new_words.usage_note: A nature walk differs from a hike in that it is slow, observational, and focused on wildlife and plants.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Nature' = prakriti + 'walk' = chalavanu → nature walk = prakriti-maa shaantthi chalo ane joi lyo.
examples: They went on a guided nature walk before settling down for their picnic.
A nature walk after lunch aids digestion and lifts the spirits.
The children spotted three different bird species on the nature walk.
She brought a wildflower guidebook along to identify plants on the nature walk.

new_words.english_meaning: A team sport played outdoors by hitting an inflated ball over a net, popular at beach and park outings.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: team sport — net uparthhi ball maarvano — beach ane park outings-maa-popular.
new_words.usage_note: A portable net and ball make it a popular activity at large group picnics; beach volleyball is a famous variant.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Volley' = utha-ane-maaro + 'ball' = dando → volleyball = net upar-thi ball maarvano game.
examples: They set up a portable net and played volleyball all afternoon.
Volleyball is a brilliant group activity for a beach outing.
She served the ball over the net to start the first game of volleyball.
The volleyball match was so competitive that nobody wanted to stop for dinner.

new_words.english_meaning: The activity of observing stars and constellations in the night sky, often done lying on a blanket outdoors.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: raatri-na-aakaash-maa-tara ane constellations-joi aanand levanu — blanket-par-suti joine.
new_words.usage_note: Best away from city lights; a simple activity requiring only a clear sky and a blanket.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Star' = taro + 'gaze' = takki-jovu → stargazing = tarao jota rehvu raat-e.
examples: They extended the outing into the evening for some stargazing.
With no city lights nearby, the stargazing was absolutely spectacular.
She brought a star chart to help identify the constellations.
Stargazing on a blanket with good company is one of life's simple pleasures.

new_words.english_meaning: The activity of riding a bicycle, often done on scenic outdoor trails or paths as part of an outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: cycle-chalavanu — scenic rastaao ke trails-par — outing-no ekk-anandmay hisso.
new_words.usage_note: Can be combined with a picnic — cycle to a scenic spot, eat, then cycle back.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Cycle' = saaik-al → cycling = cycle-chalavanu → picnic spot-sudhi cycle-thi javo.
examples: They went cycling through the countryside before stopping for a lakeside picnic.
Cycling is a fun and healthy way to explore a new outdoor area.
She hired a bicycle from the park's rental shop for the afternoon.
The cycling trail wound through beautiful forest and meadows.

new_words.english_meaning: An outdoor fire lit in a safe spot for warmth, cooking, or socialising on an outing or camping trip.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: suurakshit jagha-e-bahar-jalaveli aag — garmi, rasvad, ane dosti-masti maate.
new_words.usage_note: Always check local regulations before lighting a campfire; fire bans are common in dry seasons.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Camp' = darbaari-vaas + 'fire' = aag → campfire = bahar jalaveli masti-ni aag.
examples: They gathered around the campfire as the sun set over the hills.
She toasted marshmallows over the campfire with the children.
The campfire stories kept everyone entertained long into the night.
Check the park's rules before lighting a campfire — some areas ban open fires.

new_words.english_meaning: The activity of making quick freehand drawings of the surrounding landscape or objects during an outing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: picnic-daramyan aasjubaaj-ni prakriti ya vastu-ni jaldi-jaldi aakruti dori — creative anand.
new_words.usage_note: A peaceful solo activity perfect for artistic members of the group while others play games.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Sketch' = aakruti dori → sketching = picnic-maa-beshine prakriti dori — creative masti.
examples: She spent the afternoon sketching the rolling hills while the others played frisbee.
Sketching outdoors is a wonderful way to slow down and really observe your surroundings.
He filled an entire notebook with sketches from their countryside outings.
Even a simple pencil and paper are enough for a satisfying session of sketching.

new_words.english_meaning: The direct light and warmth from the sun, considered ideal for outdoor picnics and outings.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: suraj-no seedho prakash ane garmi — picnic mast hava-maa — best weather condition.
new_words.usage_note: Used both literally and idiomatically — 'You are my sunshine' means someone who brings happiness.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Sun' = suraj + 'shine' = chamakvu → sunshine = suraj-no chamakto prakash → picnic-ni mast hava.
examples: The picnic was perfect — hours of glorious sunshine and not a cloud in sight.
She sat with her eyes closed, simply basking in the warm sunshine.
Sunshine makes even an ordinary park look magical.
After a week of rain, the sunshine on Saturday felt like a gift.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing wind that blows in sudden, strong bursts rather than steadily.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-pavan jo vaaranghevaar achaanek tej jhatka-maa aave — shaant nahi, vaaranghevaar.
new_words.usage_note: Gusty conditions make kite-flying fun but can blow away napkins and picnic covers.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Gust' = pavan-no achaanek jhatko → gusty = achaanek-achaanek-no tej pavan.
examples: The gusty wind kept blowing the paper plates off the table.
It was a beautiful but gusty day — perfect for kite-flying.
Hold onto your hat — it's getting quite gusty out there!
Gusty conditions on the hilltop made the picnic a bit challenging.

new_words.english_meaning: The time of day just after sunset when the light is fading but it is not yet fully dark.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: suryaast-baad-no samay — jyaare aakash-no prakash mand pade chhe pan-haju raat-naahi.
new_words.usage_note: A picnic that runs until dusk is memorable for the warm golden light and cooler temperatures.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Dusk' = suryaast-baad-ni sandhyaa → dusk = din-raat-ni sandhivela — sundar rang.
examples: They stayed until dusk, watching the sky turn shades of pink and orange.
At dusk, the temperature dropped and they finally felt comfortable.
The picnic stretched from noon until dusk — an unforgettable day.
Mosquitoes tend to come out at dusk, so pack your insect repellent.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing air or weather that is unpleasantly warm, damp, and humid, making it feel suffocating.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-hava jo garm ane bhejvali hoi — uncomfortable-feeling — sweat vadhare aave.
new_words.usage_note: Common in tropical and monsoon climates; a muggy day makes an outdoor picnic feel more tiring.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Muggy' = garm-ane-bhejvali hava → muggy day = paseena-vale picnic — cooler jaruri!
examples: It was a muggy afternoon and everyone felt drained before the picnic even began.
The muggy air made it hard to stay comfortable sitting in the sun.
Bring extra cold water on muggy days — dehydration happens quickly.
A light shade cloth made all the difference on the muggy summer afternoon.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing a sky that is completely covered with clouds, blocking direct sunlight without necessarily raining.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-aakash jo vaadate badha-j-vaadallo-thi dhakayelo hoi — seedho suraj-prakash na aave.
new_words.usage_note: An overcast day can actually be ideal for a picnic — no harsh sun, still pleasant temperature.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Over' = upar + 'cast' = phailayelu → overcast = vaadalla-e-aakash dhaki lidhu.
examples: The sky was overcast but dry — perfect conditions for a comfortable picnic.
Don't cancel just because it's overcast; the soft light is actually lovely.
An overcast morning gave way to beautiful sunshine by the afternoon.
The overcast sky kept the temperature mild and pleasant all day.

new_words.english_meaning: Noticeably cold enough to feel uncomfortable without warm clothing, but not freezing.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: thodi thand — jacket vaghar-na-chhuttu — par-dhadhatho thand naahi — bahaar uncomfortable.
new_words.usage_note: Often used for mornings and evenings; 'There's a chill in the air' is a very common expression.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Chilly' = thodi thand → chilly morning = sweater-laavo → picnic-maa jacket-sathe-jao.
examples: The morning was chilly, so they wrapped up in jackets before heading out.
Bring a warm layer — evenings by the lake can get quite chilly.
Despite the chilly start, it warmed up beautifully by midday.
A chilly breeze came off the river, which was actually quite refreshing.

new_words.english_meaning: Scattered, irregular areas of cloud in the sky, alternating with patches of blue sky and sunshine.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aakash-maa-thodhaa-thodhaa vaadalla — vaachhe-vaachhe nilun aakash ane sunshine.
new_words.usage_note: Common in weather forecasts; picnic days with patchy cloud are often very pleasant as the cloud provides natural shade.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Patchy' = aw-thodhaa-thodhaa → patchy cloud = aw-vaadalla pachi-sunshine — picnic-mast.
examples: The forecast said patchy cloud, which turned out to be ideal picnic weather.
Patchy cloud meant they got some sun and some shade throughout the day.
With patchy cloud, the temperature stayed comfortable all afternoon.
She kept an eye on the patchy clouds in case they gathered into rain.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing weather that is moderately warm and calm, with no extremes of temperature or precipitation.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-havaaman jo na vadhare garm-na-vadhare thand — saamaanya ane aaaraamdaayak.
new_words.usage_note: Mild is the ideal descriptor for a perfect picnic day — not too hot, not too cold.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Mild' = majhyam — na garm na thand → mild day = perfect picnic day.
examples: The weather was mild and sunny — a perfect day for an outing.
March brings mild temperatures that are just right for outdoor dining.
Even in November, the climate here is mild enough for a picnic.
A mild breeze made the afternoon feel absolutely perfect.

new_words.english_meaning: A brief, light spell of rain that typically passes quickly, as opposed to heavy or continuous rainfall.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: thodi-varr-maat-raa-ni halki varsha — jaldi-thi-pasar-thai-jaay — varasaad-nahi-pun-thodi-varsha.
new_words.usage_note: In British English, 'a shower' almost always refers to a brief rain event; 'scattered showers' means short bursts throughout the day.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Shower' = thodi varsha → scattered showers = thodi-thodi-ne-jaldi-pass-thai-jaay varasaad.
examples: There might be a shower or two, but it should clear up by lunchtime.
A passing shower kept them under the tree for about ten minutes.
The forecast showed scattered showers, so they packed a waterproof jacket.
Don't let a brief shower put you off — it rarely lasts long.

new_words.english_meaning: The period shortly after sunrise or just before sunset when sunlight is soft, warm, and golden-coloured.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: suryoday-baad ke suryaast-pahela-no samay — jyaare suraj-no prakash garam-sona-jevo ane komal hoi.
new_words.usage_note: Beloved by photographers; timing a picnic for golden hour creates stunning photos and a magical atmosphere.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Golden' = sona-jevo + 'hour' = samay → golden hour = suraj-ni sundar-aaphi-roshni-no samay.
examples: They timed their hilltop picnic to enjoy the golden hour before sunset.
The golden hour light made every photograph from the outing look stunning.
Nothing beats sitting outdoors during golden hour with good food and friends.
She packed up just before golden hour so they could watch the sky change colour.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing an experience that restores energy, freshness, and vitality, making you feel renewed.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-anubhav jo taazgi ane urja paacho aape — thaakyu man-tantu-fari-taaju thay.
new_words.usage_note: A slightly formal adjective, but natural in reviews and personal accounts of a particularly refreshing outing.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Rejuvenate' = fari-navanuu → rejuvenating picnic = thakelo man fari-taazu — juvaan-jevi feeling.
examples: The day-long picnic in the hills was thoroughly rejuvenating.
She came back from the outing feeling rejuvenated and ready for the week ahead.
There is something deeply rejuvenating about spending a full day in nature.
A rejuvenating break outdoors can do more good than any spa treatment.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing something so special or remarkable that it is easily and fondly remembered.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-khaas-anubhav — je etlu-sundar-hoi ke yaadagaar-bani-jaay — bhulatu naahi.
new_words.usage_note: Very versatile — can describe a meal, a view, a conversation, or an entire day out.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Memory' = yaad + 'able' = karva-yogya → memorable = yaadgaar — bhulatu naahi.
examples: It was the most memorable picnic we had ever been on.
The sunset view from the hilltop made the whole day truly memorable.
She created a scrapbook of the outing to preserve the memorable moments.
Memorable experiences are made by the people you share them with.

new_words.english_meaning: Calm, peaceful, and undisturbed — describing a place or atmosphere that inspires quiet contentment.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: shaant, aanandmay ane nishchal — aw-jaga ya vataavaran je man-ne-chain-aape.
new_words.usage_note: Often used to describe natural settings like lakesides and forests; a go-to word in travel and lifestyle writing.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Serene' = shaant ane nishchal → serene picnic spot = jyaa man ek-dam chain maane.
examples: The forest glade was so serene that nobody wanted to break the silence.
She described the hilltop picnic as serene and utterly restorative.
A serene setting makes even simple food taste more delicious.
The serene atmosphere of the orchard instantly calmed her busy mind.

new_words.english_meaning: Happening or done without prior planning, on a sudden natural impulse.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: pehela-thi-aayojan-vagar — achaanek-j-mun-thayu ane nikli-pddya — tatkalik-no-anubhav.
new_words.usage_note: Often used positively to describe outings that turned out wonderfully despite zero planning.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Spontaneous' = achaanek-no vichar → spontaneous picnic = 'Chalo, aajej jaiyu!' — pehela-na-plan-vagar.
examples: The spontaneous picnic after the morning market was the best part of the trip.
She loved spontaneous outings — they always turned out to be the most fun.
It was a completely spontaneous decision to drive to the countryside that afternoon.
Some of the most memorable days are the spontaneous ones.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing an activity or experience that is good, healthy, and morally positive — leaving you feeling complete.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-pramaanik ane swasthya-purna anubhav — je man-ane-tan-ne-saro-feel-karaave.
new_words.usage_note: Used to describe activities that are good for the spirit and bring families or friends together positively.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Whole' = pooru + 'some' = some → wholesome = pooru-ane-saacha — man-tan-mast-raakhe.
examples: A family picnic is the most wholesome way to spend a weekend afternoon.
There is something deeply wholesome about eating food you cooked yourself outdoors.
The children's laughter made the whole outing feel truly wholesome.
She described the weekend trip to the countryside as wholesome and restorative.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing a place or situation that is extremely peaceful, beautiful, and ideally suited to happiness.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-jaga ya parithiti je bilkul-shaant, sundar ane aanand-maate-made-for — swarg-jaisi.
new_words.usage_note: A higher-register word; used in travel writing and personal essays to describe a perfect, almost dreamlike setting.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Idyllic' = swarg-jaisi sundarata → idyllic picnic spot = jyaa jaao to din-yadgaar bani jaay.
examples: The orchard in bloom was an idyllic setting for their anniversary picnic.
She described the afternoon as idyllic — warm sun, good food, and great company.
Finding an idyllic spot by the stream made all the planning worthwhile.
The waterfront at golden hour was nothing short of idyllic.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing a warm, friendly, and lively atmosphere created by people enjoying each other's company.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-garm ane maitripoorn vataavaran — jyaa log ek-bee-sathe aanandthi-bethe-hoi — dosti-no aanand.
new_words.usage_note: A slightly formal adjective; commonly found in restaurant and event reviews.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Con' = saath + 'vivial' = jeevant → convivial = saath-maa-jeevant ane mast — dosti-bhari masti.
examples: The picnic had a wonderfully convivial atmosphere — everyone was relaxed and laughing.
Good food and open air always create a convivial mood.
The convivial gathering stretched well into the evening.
There is nothing like a potluck picnic to generate a truly convivial spirit.

new_words.english_meaning: Describing something that makes you feel energetic, alert, and full of life.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-anubhav jo urja ane chalakpan aape — tan-man-ne-uthaan-aave — fresh feeling.
new_words.usage_note: Often collocates with fresh air, cold water, or a brisk walk — all common elements of outdoor outings.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Invigorate' = urja bharo → invigorating = aw-kriya je tanmanma-navi-urja-bhere — fresh feel.
examples: The brisk nature walk before breakfast was invigorating for everyone.
Cold fresh air from the hills felt deeply invigorating after the city's pollution.
She found the paddling in the stream surprisingly invigorating.
An invigorating morning outdoors sets a positive tone for the whole day.

new_words.english_meaning: Moving or proceeding calmly without rush or pressure, allowing time to enjoy each moment fully.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: aw-jaldi-vagar — aaraampurvak — drek-pal-maanvanu — koi-pressure-vagar-shaant-reetho.
new_words.usage_note: A picnic done at an unhurried pace is considered the ideal — no agenda, no clock-watching.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Un' = na + 'hurried' = jaldi → unhurried = jaldi-vagar — maje-maje-aage-vadhvu.
examples: They spent an unhurried afternoon at the waterfront, with nowhere to be.
The best picnics are unhurried — you eat when you're hungry and leave when you're ready.
She loved the unhurried pace of their countryside outing.
An unhurried morning walk before the picnic set a perfectly relaxed tone.

new_words.english_meaning: Deeply absorbed in and surrounded by the natural environment, feeling completely at one with the outdoors.
new_words.gujarati_meaning: prakruti-maa-tamam ane poora-j-dubhu — sheher-bhulayelu — ane prakruti-sathe-ekroop thayelu.
new_words.usage_note: Used to express a profound connection with the natural environment rather than simply being outdoors.
new_words.memory_tip: 'Immersed' = dubhu → immersed in nature = prakruti-maa-pooro-dubhu — sheher bhulayelu.
examples: Spending a whole day in the forest left her feeling completely immersed in nature.
The children were so immersed in nature that they forgot about their phones entirely.
Being immersed in nature for even one day can dramatically reduce stress levels.
The best picnics leave you feeling truly immersed in nature rather than just visiting it.
